affected_boundaries: normalized records to transactional PostgreSQL search publication

observed_behavior: A full 212,720-record build took 118,941 ms, dominated by per-record search writes and updates of unchanged immutable text rows.
expected_behavior: Publish large generations in tens of seconds while preserving atomicity and unchanged content.
causal_mechanism: Search publication used two awaited SQL statements for every row and a conflict update for text already addressed by its content hash.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A bulk immutable publication was expressed as repeated individual mutable upserts.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Round trips and unnecessary physical tuple updates accumulate with every record.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Text is reused by content hash; bounded publication batches remain inside the original transaction and report completed writes only.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Stream sorted search documents through batches bounded by rows and parameter bytes, insert text with conflict-ignore and upsert search metadata.

applicability_conditions: Large normalized generations and a shared content-addressed text table.
known_non_matches: An unchanged generation bypasses record publication and reuses its existing generation.
confirmation_evidence: The physical tuple regression failed before the repair and passed afterward.
The same isolated workload fell from 118,941 to 46,100 ms; an unchanged update took 4,843 ms.
